name: Jehozadak
overview: Jehozadak, also known as Josedech or Jozadak, was a priest taken into captivity when the LORD allowed Judah and Jerusalem to be carried away by Nebuchadnezzar, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:14-15. He is notably mentioned as the father of Jeshua (Jeshua), who, along with Zerubbabel and other priests and Levites, played a key role in rebuilding the altar and the house of God upon their return from exile (Ezra 3:2, 3:8, 5:2). The legacy of Jehozadak’s priestly line continued despite challenges, including the issue of intermarriage among his descendants (Ezra 10:18), emphasizing the faithfulness and restoration of God’s covenant people through the priesthood after the exile.
